title: Relate — Spring 2026
coverLines: Thirteen weeks to a faithful family
summary: Spring 2026 family study guide from Relate: thirteen weeks of daily grace around one household — a verse and a daily read for every day of the season. Because the mercies are new every morning.

blocks.text: How to use this study guide

This is a Relate study guide for the whole household. Spring has thirteen weeks, and each week we practise one home-habit — first light, the welcome table, grace for messes, good words, enough, brave hearts — until the mornings themselves do the reminding. Each day has a verse to read aloud, two or three lines to think about, a small Try it step, and a prayer to say together.
New every morning

A family does not get faithful in one sitting. It gets faithful one morning at a time — coffee, breakfast, one verse, one honest conversation, one small kindness. God's mercy is new every morning, which means there is always enough grace for today. We don't need to be strong for the whole season; we only need to be faithful for today.

Follow the steps on each day: read the verse, read the lines, do the Try it, then say the prayer together. On day 5 of each week there is a short quiz to remember what you practised. On days 6 and 7 you get to rest and reflect — talk it over, or write it down on your own. At the end of spring you will have built a home where the mercies come like the morning.

intro.text: Before breakfast, before the lists, before the noise — there is first light. The season opens with the simplest of all habits: letting God's new mercies meet you at the top of the day.

verse.text: And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light.

blocks.text: The very first thing God does in the Bible is speak light into the dark. Light is what makes a beginning possible — you can't see where you're going, what's in the room, or who's beside you without it. Every day of this season is a small beginning, and God is already speaking light into it before you wake.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Wake the first light habit: nobody looks at a screen before the verse is read
Open the curtains and read today's verse aloud together
Name one thing you're starting fresh today

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for a new day and new light
Ask Him to speak light into your home this spring

verse.text: They are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.

blocks.text: Jeremiah wrote this in the ruins of a broken city, in the worst season of his life. And still he saw it: God's mercy is not saved up for grand moments — it arrives fresh every single morning, like bread from the oven. Whatever yesterday's failures were, today has its own full supply of grace.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Start the day by saying the one-word prayer: 'Mercies.'
Let yesterday's mistakes stay in yesterday's jar — don't bring them to the breakfast table
Ask each person: what is one mercy you've seen today?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that His mercy is new today
Confess yesterday's failure and leave it with Him

verse.text: Weeping may stay for the night, but rejoicing comes in the morning.

blocks.text: Some nights in a home are heavy — a hard conversation, a bad report, a worried heart that keeps everyone awake. The psalmist does not pretend sadness isn't real. He just knows the truth about the next 24 hours: God's mercy turns the corner, and joy genuinely does come back in the morning.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: If last night was heavy, let this morning be the correction: a fresh start and a clean hug
Tell a child the promise: 'sadness has a bedtime, but joy comes in the morning'
Choose one small joy to put first — music, a walk, a favourite breakfast

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for joy to return to a tired heart today
Thank Him that sadness is not the end of the story

days.title: A new heart for the season

verse.text: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!

blocks.text: A new season is a gift because it reminds us that God is in the business of fresh starts. New creation was never a one-time event — every day in Christ you get to be the newest version of yourself. The 'new' God does in you also shapes what your home can become this spring.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Write the word 'new' somewhere you'll see it every morning this week
Choose one old habit the family is leaving in the old season
Pick one new habit to grow in its place

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make each of you new in Christ today
Thank Him that the old is gone

verse.text: See, I am doing a new thing! Now it springs up; do you not perceive it?

blocks.text: God doesn't just give you a new day — He is actively doing a new thing in it. The problem is we often don't perceive it because we're staring at what used to be. Today's quiz is about seeing what God is up to that you might have missed.

blocks.question: In Isaiah 43:19, where is God doing His new thing?
options: In the desert — in the unlikely, dry places
Only in the comfortable, easy seasons
blocks.explain: Right — the new thing springs up 'in the desert'. God often starts with the driest ground in your home and quietly waters it.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to open your eyes to His new thing this spring
Thank Him for the work He is already doing

days.title: The day the Lord has made

verse.text: The LORD has done it this very day; let us rejoice and be glad in it.

blocks.text: Sunday is God's gift of rest — a whole day that needs no production. Psalm 118 doesn't say 'he rejoiced in it'; it hands you the day and tells you to be glad in it too. Rest that rejoices is part of faithful family life, not a break from it.

blocks.prompt: What is one way you can rest today that actually restores you? Write it down, or tell the family what you'd choose.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive today as a gift from God
Thank Him for rest in the middle of a busy season

verse.text: God saw all that he had made, and it was very good.

blocks.text: The first week of the Bible ends with God looking at everything and calling it 'very good'. He is not a distant critic of your home; He is a creator who loves what He is still making of you. To begin a season well, begin with this: Monday, receive your home as God's good gift.

blocks.prompt: Look around your household today. What is one 'very good' thing God has made in this family? Write it down or say it out loud.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the good He has made in your family
Ask Him to keep making you 'very good' this spring

intro.text: A faithful family is not a family with no arguments — it is a family that has practised dwelling together when it's easy and when it isn't. This week we build the habits that hold a household together.

verse.text: How good and pleasant it is when God's people live together in unity!

blocks.text: David puts unity at the top of God's 'good and pleasant' list. Not impressive, not busy, not perfect — good and pleasant. Food tastes better, evenings go quieter, and the home runs lighter when the people under one roof are pulling together instead of across each other.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Say 'we' when you talk about a problem — we're in this together
Do one chore you normally wouldn't, for someone else
End the day with one sentence of thank-you to someone in the house

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for unity that is good and pleasant in your home
Thank Him for the people under your roof

verse.text: For where two or three gather in my name, there am I with them.

blocks.text: Jesus doesn't wait for a full house. He promises His presence to two or three. That means your smallest, messiest gathering — a verse with cereal bowls, a prayer in the car — is a real meeting with Jesus. You do not need more people; you need to gather in His name.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Gather two or three anywhere: a verse at breakfast, a prayer in the car
Begin the gathering with Jesus' name out loud
Don't cancel it because it's small — that's exactly the size He loves

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank Jesus that He meets you even in a gathered two or three
Ask Him to feel near in your small moments today

verse.text: Bear with each other and forgive one another if any of you has a grievance against someone.

blocks.text: 'Bear with' is a picture of holding a load together — like two people carrying a heavy piece of furniture through a doorway. Family life is a lot of load-bearing. The call isn't to never annoy each other; it's to keep carrying for each other even when the weight shifts.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Notice one strength in someone who often irritates you — say it out loud
When you feel the load shift, take a deep breath before you speak
Forgive a small grievance today before it becomes a big one

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for patience to bear with one another
Forgive your family as God in Christ forgave you

days.title: As for me and my house

verse.text: As for me and my household, we will serve the LORD.

blocks.text: Joshua makes the bravest statement a parent can make: not 'everyone might serve God someday' but 'as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.' A household needs an honest direction, and this is the one worth setting — out loud, where everyone can be steadied by it.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Declare Joshua's words out loud at a meal — and mean them
Decide together: what does serving the LORD look like in your house this week?
Make the decision visible: a small sign or a saved spot for the verse

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Make the family decision: we will serve the LORD
Ask Him to help you keep that promise

days.title: A home that answers the call

verse.text: Be completely humble and gentle; be patient, bearing with one another in love.

blocks.text: Paul stacks the operating manual of a household: humility, gentleness, patience, bearing, love. Today's quiz is a quick check on which fuel runs your evening.

blocks.question: Which fuel keeps a family hummable all week: pride, or humility?
options: Pride — 'I'm right, and I'll prove it'
Humility — 'we're learning to be gentle together'
blocks.explain: Right — pride slams doors; humility opens them. Humble and gentle is the only engine that runs quietly enough for a family to sleep.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for a humble heart in your own home
Thank Him that patience with you never runs out

verse.text: Where you go I will go, and where you stay I will stay.

blocks.text: Ruth says these words to her mother-in-law — a family bond that holds even after the easy reasons are gone. Loyalty is not a feeling; it is a decision you keep repeating. On a rest day, let the family rest in knowing they are kept, and keeping.

blocks.prompt: Who in your household do you promise to stay with, no matter what? Write it, draw it, or just say it out loud today.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the loyal people in your life
Ask Him to make you a faithful keeper of family

verse.text: Start children off on the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not turn from it.

blocks.text: This is a promise about direction, not perfection. When you point a child toward God's way — honestly, patiently, over years — you are doing something God protects. Monday is the day to think long: the small habits of this season are the shape of someone's whole road.

blocks.prompt: What is one 'way' you are pointing someone in your household toward Jesus? How will you keep pointing that way this season?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Lift up the children of your household to God
Ask Him to keep them on His way for life

intro.text: Some of the most important things God does happen at tables. This week we practise the habit of welcome — making room at the table for one more, especially for the person nobody else thinks to invite.

verse.text: Share with the Lord's people who are in need. Practice hospitality.

blocks.text: Paul links two habits that belong together: sharing and hospitality. Hospitality is not catering; it is the courage to say 'there is room for you here.' And the first people on the list are the ones in need — the lonely, the new, the struggling. Practice it: the word means it gets better the more you do it.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Look at your table and ask: who could fit one more?
Invite one person — a neighbour, a new family — for something simple this week
Remember: welcome is practice, not perfection

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to show you someone to welcome
Thank Him for the table of His grace

verse.text: Do not forget to show hospitality to strangers, for by so doing some people have shown hospitality to angels without knowing it.

blocks.text: The writer's point is not that every stranger is an angel — it's that hospitality is bigger than we can see. When you welcome a person, you are really welcoming God's work into your home. You often won't know until later what the visit meant, or who was actually sent to whom.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Welcome the stranger: a delivery person, a new colleague, a shy visitor
Offer something small and warm — water, a seat, a few minutes
Expect nothing back; that's the whole point

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to send you the people He wants at your table
Thank Him for hosting you, a stranger welcomed home

verse.text: When you give a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind.

blocks.text: Jesus draws the guest list of His kingdom, and it is a reversal. Not the people who can repay you — the people who can't. This isn't about becoming gloomy; it's about becoming free. When you stop inviting for return, you start hosting for joy, and the table becomes a truly wide place.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Make one meal this week for someone who cannot repay you
Enjoy it — great generosity is supposed to be great fun
Ask: who in our town is 'the poor, the lame, the blind'?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the upside-down kingdom where the last are first
Ask Him to give you the joy of giving without return

verse.text: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them.

blocks.text: Long before Jesus, Israel was told: the foreigner living among you is not a threat to manage but a person to protect. The heart of welcome is standing against the mean instinct — the instinct to make outsiders feel that they don't belong. Your home can be a place where people breathe out.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Notice who is 'the outsider' in your neighbourhood or school
Choose kindness toward them deliberately today
Watch your words — the ones that make people feel left out

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to search your heart for who you leave out
Thank Him for welcoming you when you were far off

days.title: My house, a house of prayer

verse.text: My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations.

blocks.text: Jesus quoted this in the temple courtyard. Your home can carry the same calling: a house where prayer is at home, and where that welcome reaches 'all nations'. Today's quiz is about the easiest test of a welcoming home.

blocks.question: Which surprise guest felt welcome in Jesus' story of the banquet (Luke 14)?
options: The friend who could repay the favour
The poor, crippled, lame and blind
blocks.explain: Right — Jesus openly names the guest list of His kingdom: the people nobody else invited.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make your home a house of prayer for all nations
Thank Him for a welcoming God

days.title: Whatever you did for one of these

verse.text: Whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.

blocks.text: On a rest day, sit with the quiet weight of this: Jesus is present in the people who can't pay you back. The cup of water for the thirsty, the time for the lonely — He receives it all as done to Him. Welcome is never wasted, because it is never just for the guest.

blocks.prompt: Think of one 'least of these' you know. What is a small welcome you can offer them this week? Write it down.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Jesus to help you see Him in the people who need welcome
Thank Him for welcoming you when you were least

verse.text: Now you are no longer a stranger but a fellow citizen with the saints and members of the household of God.

blocks.text: The best welcome story is your own. Before you were a family member, you were a stranger, and God made you a fellow citizen at His table. Monday is a good day to welcome others the way you were welcomed — because you remember what it felt like to be let in.

blocks.prompt: Remember when God welcomed you in. How did it feel? Write it down, then choose one person to welcome this week in the same way.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that you are no longer a stranger
Ask Him to make your home a welcoming household

intro.text: Every household makes messes — spilled words, spilled milk, broken trust. The question is not whether the mess will come; it is whether grace will be ready for it. This week we practise the family habit of forgiveness.

verse.text: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, "Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother or sister who sins against me? Up to seven times?" Jesus answered, "I tell you, not seven times, but seventy-seven times."

blocks.text: Peter thought he was being generous; Jesus was being glorious. Not seven but seventy-seven — in other words, stop counting. Grace doesn't keep a tally. In a family, forgiveness is not a policy; it is the air you breathe so no one suffocates.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Drop the tally: erase one grudge you were keeping score on
Say the words yourself: 'I forgive you' and 'I need your forgiveness'
Give someone a win today even though they wronged you

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for the strength to forgive without counting
Thank Him that His forgiveness of you is uncountable

verse.text: Forgive as the Lord forgave you.

blocks.text: The standard is not 'forgive them if they apologise nicely' or 'forgive them when they prove they've changed'. It is: forgive as the Lord forgave you — first, fully, undeserved. That is a giant forgiveness, and it's the only one big enough for a whole household.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Forgive someone before they finish apologising — be first
Reflect on the size of your own forgiveness, then release theirs
Ask the Holy Spirit to loosen any knot of unforgiveness in you

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank Christ for the way He forgave you
Ask for His grace to forgive the same way

verse.text: But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion for him; he ran to his son, threw his arms around him and kissed him.

blocks.text: The father doesn't wait for his son to come all the way home. He runs the impossible distance and meets him — with compassion, arms, a kiss. That's the pattern for grace in your home: you don't wait for the mess to be fully cleaned before you love. You run toward the person.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Run toward someone who is far off today — the distance is shorter than you think
Greet them with compassion, not a lecture
Remember: they are not their mess

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that He runs to you when you're far off
Ask Him for a father-heart toward the wanderers in your life

verse.text: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

blocks.text: Messes are often made worse by the first spoken response. A gentle answer is not weakness — it is the skill of turning a fire down instead of feeding it. In the heat of the moment, your first job is not to be right. It is to be gentle.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Practice your slow-down: one breath before any hot reply
Turn a harsh word down to a gentle one — feel the difference
If you already said the harsh word, go back and say the sweet one

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to guard your tongue around your family
Thank Him for the peace a soft answer brings

verse.text: So watch yourselves. "If your brother or sister sins against you, rebuke them; and if they repent, forgive them."

blocks.text: Jesus doesn't ignore the mess — He gives a way to clean it: a gentle rebuke, then forgiveness when they turn. Today's quiz tests which habit actually rebuilds a mess-damaged home.

blocks.question: What makes forgiveness real in a family, according to Luke 17:3?
options: Forgetting it ever happened
A gentle rebuke, then real forgiveness when they repent
blocks.explain: Right — Jesus teaches both honesty and release. Hiding the mess and smothering the forgiveness don't rebuild trust; truth followed by grace does.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for the courage to speak truth gently
Thank Him for forgiving you every time you repent

verse.text: Above all, love each other deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins.

blocks.text: Love covers — it does not expose, parade or weaponise. In a home, the deep love that forgives quietly is what keeps the walls standing. On a rest day, let this sink in: the family that knows it is covered is the family that is free to be honest.

blocks.prompt: Is there an old mess you keep re-exposing? Write it down as a release — then let love cover it.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to cover the sins in your home with love
Thank Him for covering yours in Christ

verse.text: Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other, just as in Christ God forgave you.

blocks.text: Paul pairs forgiveness with its two travelling companions: kindness and compassion. You don't forgive generically; you forgive as a kind, compassionate person who remembers exactly how it feels to need grace. That is the shape of a family that survives its messes.

blocks.prompt: This week had messes, and grace for them. Write one sentence of thanks to God for a specific forgiveness — given or received.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive God's kindness and compassion toward you
Ask Him to make you kind and compassionate when others fail

intro.text: Words build homes or hollow them out. This week we practise the habit of good words — words that bless, build and tell the truth in love, spoken slowly enough to mean.

verse.text: Let your conversation be always full of grace, seasoned with salt.

blocks.text: Salt preserves and sharpens taste. Grace-seasoned words are words that keep the household healthy and give it flavour — not bland, not bitter, never stale. Before you speak to someone under your own roof, ask the one question: full of grace?

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Run your words through the gate: is this full of grace?
Add some salt — make one conversation honest and alive, not just nice
Bless someone with your voice on purpose today

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to season your words with grace today
Thank Him for the way His Word gives flavour to life

verse.text: The tongue has the power of life and death.

blocks.text: One small muscle, running one huge errand. Words have actually ended and begun lives — marriages held up, children wrecked or raised, hope handed across a room. Every day you speak life or death into the people under your roof. There is no neutral option.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Speak one sentence of pure life to each person in your home
Before a critical word, decide: will this heal or hurt?
Interrupt a negative phrase mid-sentence and turn it toward life

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make your mouth a life-giving place
Confess the words that brought death and ask for repair

verse.text: Do not let any unwholesome talk come out of your mouths, but only what is helpful for building others up according to their needs.

blocks.text: Paul sets the bar not at 'nothing bad' but at 'something good for building up.' The mission of family words is constructive. Speak according to their needs — the exact encouragement, the precise thanks, the word someone was starving for.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Study your family: what does each person need to hear right now?
Say it — specifically, out loud, today
Starve one unwholesome habit of conversation

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for words tailored to each person's need
Thank Him for every word that builds you up

verse.text: Listen to advice and accept discipline, and in the end you will be counted among the wise.

blocks.text: Good words include good listening. Wisdom begins not when you give advice but when you take it — from a parent, a spouse, a child, a friend. A household that listens to correction grows in every generation.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Ask one person in your home for advice — and actually take it
Receive a correction today without defending yourself
Let a child teach you something

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for a listening heart that accepts discipline
Thank Him for the wise people He has placed around you

verse.text: But the wisdom that comes from heaven is first of all pure; then peace-loving, considerate, submissive, full of mercy.

blocks.text: James says wisdom is distinguishable by its flavour: pure, then peace-loving, considerate, full of mercy. Today's quiz checks which word actually tastes like the kingdom.

blocks.question: Which of these words is 'full of mercy' from heaven's perspective?
options: The surgical put-down that leaves a bruise
The considerate word that leaves a door open
blocks.explain: Right — heavenly wisdom is considerate and mercy-full, not cutting. The right word leaves hope in the room.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for wisdom from above in your words
Thank Him for every gentle, truthful word spoken to you

verse.text: The Sovereign LORD has given me a well-instructed tongue, to know the word that sustains the weary.

blocks.text: Isaiah's vision for a tongue: not impressive, but well-instructed — taught to know the exact word that sustains a weary person. Every family has a weary one. On a rest day, ask God which word theirs is today.

blocks.prompt: Who in your home is most weary right now? Learn the word that sustains them, and speak it today. Write the word down.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for a well-instructed tongue
Bring the weary person in your home before Him

verse.text: A person finds joy in giving an apt reply — and how good is a timely word!

blocks.text: A timely word is a gift you give at exactly the right moment. Timing is part of grace: encouragement when someone is about to give up, thanks before it's too late, a sorry spoken quickly. Monday is for timely words — say them today, while they still land.

blocks.prompt: Is there a word you've been meaning to say but haven't? Say it today — and write down how it went.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the joy of apt replies
Ask Him to help you speak every timely word this week

intro.text: Spring teaching on 'enough': a household that knows God provides learns the calm of contentment — not more, not less, but enough. This week we practise trusting the Provider.

verse.text: The LORD is my shepherd, I lack nothing.

blocks.text: Psalm 23 opens with the quietest of claims: with the LORD as shepherd, I lack nothing. Not 'I lack only the expensive things.' Nothing. That is not a promise of riches; it is a promise of enough — and it is the foundation of every calm household.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Say it out loud with meaning: 'The LORD is my shepherd, I lack nothing.'
List three things you have that are exactly enough today
Notice one thing you were about to wish away — and thank God for it

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that He is your Shepherd and you lack nothing
Ask Him to quiet your wanting heart

verse.text: The people eat their fill, and each gathered as much as they needed.

blocks.text: In the desert God gave Israel one day's bread at a time. Gathering more than needed produced nothing but rot — greed literally spoiled. God was teaching a whole nation the rhythm of enough: trust Me for today; there will be enough tomorrow.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Live on 'manna rules': trust God for today's needs
When anxiety about tomorrow knocks, counter with a fact of today's provision
Give something away — the surest sign you believe in enough

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for today's bread and today's peace
Thank Him that He knows your needs before you ask

verse.text: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself.

blocks.text: Jesus is blunt: worry does not add a single hour to life; it subtracts a day of it. He points to the birds and the flowers — fed and clothed without a shred of anxiety — and calls worry what it is: a small faith problem, cured by a big God.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Give tomorrow's problems a later appointment — today is off limits
Feed a bird, look at a flower, and receive the lesson
When worry comes, trade it for a specific prayer

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Hand today's worries to God one by one
Thank Him for His care for the birds — and you

verse.text: But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.

blocks.text: The order is everything. Put God's kingdom first, and the 'these things' — food, clothes, the small daily provisions — follow like ducklings. When a household puts the kingdom first, its possessions stop owning it, and enough stops feeling like not enough.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Start the day asking: what does the kingdom need from me today?
Put a need down and watch God provide it in His order
Practise the reverse: before the bills, the Kingdom.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to reorder your first things today
Thank Him that the kingdom comes with provision

verse.text: I have learned the secret of being content in any and every situation, whether well fed or hungry.

blocks.text: Paul says contentment is a secret he learned — a skill, practised like any other. Today's quiz is about where that secret is found.

blocks.question: Where did Paul discover the secret of contentment?
options: In having everything he ever wanted
In Christ, who strengthens him in every situation
blocks.explain: Right — Paul goes on to say 'I can do all this through him who gives me strength.' Contentment is not circumstances; it is Christ.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Christ for the secret, learned secret of contentment
Thank Him for strength in every situation

verse.text: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field... will he not much more clothe you?

blocks.text: Jesus argues upward from small to great: the grass is dressed in glory one morning and gone the next — and you are worth more than all of it. On a rest day, let the argument land: the God who dresses the fields is the God who has not forgotten you.

blocks.prompt: Think of one provision God has given you that felt impossible. Write it down and give thanks for the Provider, not just the provision.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for clothing the fields and caring for you
Ask Him to still your anxious heart

verse.text: And my God will meet all your needs according to the riches of his glory in Christ Jesus.

blocks.text: Paul ends the 'enough' chapter with a cheque drawn on heaven's bank: all your needs, according to His riches, in Christ Jesus. Our needs have a known source and a full supply. Monday is the day to lower the anchor of the whole house into that promise.

blocks.prompt: Paul filled your week with 'enough'. Write one way God met a need this week that you didn't see coming.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive the promise: God will meet all your needs
Thank Him in advance for the supply of this day

intro.text: Fear is the oldest enemy of family calm. This week we arm the household with courage — the Bible's word for it is 'be strong and courageous', and it is always built on the same two rails: God is with you, and He has already gone ahead.

verse.text: Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged, for the LORD your God will be with you wherever you go.

blocks.text: Joshua is standing at the edge of a whole new life, and God gives him the family anthem of every generation: be strong and courageous — not because the way ahead is easy, but because God will be with you wherever you go. Courage is not the absence of fear; it is fear that has heard the promise.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Say Joshua 1:9 aloud to one person in your home
Name the fear, then name the promise beside it
Do one brave small thing you've been delaying

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for courage for the family's road ahead
Thank Him that He goes with you wherever you go

days.title: The LORD your God, the warrior

verse.text: The LORD your God is with you... he will quiet you with his love.

blocks.text: Zephaniah gives fear the best answer: the mighty LORD saves you, rejoices over you, and quiets you with His love. The same God who is mighty is also tender — He doesn't shout fear away; He calms it with love. That is a brave heart's fuel.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Visualise God quieting your heart with His love instead of loud noise
Let that calm be the tone of one conversation today
Repeat the phrase when fear spikes: 'He quieted me with His love'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to quiet your heart with His love
Thank Him that He rejoices over you

days.title: Do not fear, I will help

verse.text: So do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God.

blocks.text: The verse continues: 'I will strengthen you and help you; I will uphold you with my righteous right hand.' Fear falls in pieces when it meets three facts: He is with you, He is your God, and His right hand is underneath you.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: List what you fear — then hold each one up to the three facts
Accept a helping hand from someone today and let them help
Be the upholding hand for one weary person

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Lay your fears before the God who upholds you
Thank Him for His righteous right hand

verse.text: But now, LORD, what do I look for? My hope is in you.

blocks.text: David's question 'what do I look for?' is the real question of courage. Fear looks for failure, betrayal, collapse. Hope looks to God — the one fixed point that cannot shake. A brave household aims its looking: my hope is in You.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Ask the question honestly: what am I actually looking for today?
Deliberately aim your hope at God, not at outcomes
Say with David: 'My hope is in you.'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to be the fixed point of your hoping
Thank Him for the hope that does not disappoint

verse.text: He said, "You of little faith, why did you doubt?"

blocks.text: Peter walks on water as long as he watches Jesus; the moment he studies the wind, he sinks. Jesus doesn't say the storm wasn't real — He says doubt was louder than the promise. Today's quiz is about where brave people keep their eyes.

blocks.question: What did Peter stop doing right before he sank?
options: He stopped looking at Jesus and looked at the wind
He stopped praying aloud in a loud voice
blocks.explain: Right — focused on the storm, not the Saviour, Peter sank. Courage is all about where your eyes live.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Jesus to order your eyes to stay on Him
Thank Him that His hand is there to catch you

verse.text: Truly my soul finds rest in God; my salvation comes from him.

blocks.text: Courage eventually needs rest, or it becomes exhaustion. David's rest is not escapism — it is a deliberate placement of his soul: into God. On a rest day, the brave thing to do is lie your worried heart down and let the Strong One stand watch.

blocks.prompt: Where is your soul currently resting — in fear, or in God? Write one fear and hand it to Him in writing.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Lay your soul down in God's safekeeping
Thank Him for salvation and rest in one package

verse.text: Wait for the LORD; be strong and take heart and wait for the LORD.

blocks.text: Psalm 27 ends with an instruction for the long road: wait for the LORD, and while you wait, be strong and take heart. Courage is not just sprinting through fears — it is the long patience of trusting God on His timetable. Monday sets your pace for the rest of the season.

blocks.prompt: Write the one thing your family is waiting on God for. Thank Him before the answer comes — that's the courage of faith.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for the strength to wait on His timing
Thank Him that the wait is held by His hand

intro.text: Growth is slow by design. This week the household practised being patient — with each other, with answers that haven't come, and with the slow, steady work God is doing in lives you can't see change yet.

verse.text: Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, faithful in prayer.

blocks.text: Paul hands out three habits as a set: joy in hope, patience in affliction, faithfulness in prayer. Notice patience isn't passive. It is the active courage of staying put when staying put is hard, kept warm by joy and held up by prayer.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Pick the one thing you're waiting on and declare it 'a joy-full hope'
Practise patience in affliction: don't grumble through one small irritation
Let prayer be the muscle that does the holding

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for joy in the hope you're waiting on
Thank Him for His patience with your own growing

verse.text: There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under the heavens.

blocks.text: The Preacher knew what every gardener knows: apples are not rushed, children are not scheduled, and answers have a season. Patience is not just surviving the wait — it is the wisdom to know which season you are in and to live it well instead of fighting it.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name the season your family is in right now
Do one thing that season actually calls for — not the one you wish it did
Trust that this season ends: there is a time for everything

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to help you live your current season well
Thank Him that He is the Lord of every season

verse.text: See how the farmer waits for the land to yield its valuable crop, patiently waiting for the autumn and spring rains.

blocks.text: James points to a farmer as the masterclass in patience: sowing, then waiting, season after season, for what he cannot hurry. The crop doesn't appear on the farmer's schedule — it appears on the land's. Faithful family life works the same way.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Do your seeding work today — then release the result to God
Water something you planted long ago, even if you can't see it
Imagine the harvest, and let hope speed the waiting

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the farmer's patience He is practising on you
Ask for patience to wait for the harvest

verse.text: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to become angry.

blocks.text: Patience with people shows up first in the mouth and the ears. Quick to listen, slow to speak, slow to anger. Around a family table this is the difference between a conversation and a collision.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Be the quickest listener at your next family conversation
Delay your reply by one full breath — be slow to speak
Give anger a longer fuse today

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for quick ears and a slow tongue
Thank Him for the patience He shows every listener

verse.text: Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.

blocks.text: Paul names the exact danger of a waiting season: weariness, giving up just before the harvest. The promise is a timetable — 'at the proper time'. Today's quiz tests the antidote to quitting.

blocks.question: What keeps a family from giving up while they wait?
options: Doing good steadily, and trusting the proper time
Checking results every single day
blocks.explain: Right — 'we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.' Check the field less; keep the good work steady.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for strength not to grow weary in doing good
Thank Him that the proper time is on His calendar

verse.text: Be still before the LORD and wait patiently for him.

blocks.text: Waiting can be done two ways: standing in a queue anxiously, or sitting before the LORD attentively. 'Be still before the LORD' turns rest day into the school where patience is learned. The stillness is not empty — He is there.

blocks.prompt: Be still for five quiet minutes — no task, no screen. What surfaces when waiting becomes meeting God? Write what you notice.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Be still before the LORD and wait patiently
Thank Him that waiting on Him never embarrasses

verse.text: Be patient, then, brothers and sisters, until the Lord's coming.

blocks.text: James ground all patience in the biggest promise: the Lord is coming, and He is close. Every hard wait in this life is a short wait on that scale. Monday lets you look past the horizon — your waiting has an end, and it is glorious.

blocks.prompt: Write one sentence of honest hope: 'I can wait, because...' Read it aloud tonight.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Set your patience on the coming of the Lord
Thank Him that He is close, especially in the waiting

intro.text: There is one habit that unclenches a whole household: generosity. This week we practise giving — time, money, house room, help — and discover that a family that gives is a family that breathes.

verse.text: God loves a cheerful giver.

blocks.text: Paul strips giving down to its engine: the heart. Not the size of the gift, not the arithmetic — the cheerfulness. A household that gives grudgingly learns to give smaller; a household that gives joyfully finds its gift is always growing.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Give something (time, money, help) with a smile on your face
Check the motive: giving from joy, or from pressure?
Let the kids choose something small to give — and celebrate the cheer

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make you a cheerful giver
Thank Him for every gift He has poured into your family

verse.text: It is more blessed to give than to receive.

blocks.text: These are Jesus' own words, preserved by Paul. The blessing of giving is not a points system — it is simply the way human hearts are wired. Givers get the joy; hoarders get the guard duty. Your family can test this one at any time.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Run the experiment: give something away, then notice how you feel
Give where nothing comes back — that's the blessed corner
Tell a child Jesus' words: 'more blessed to give than to receive'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Jesus to teach you His blessed way of giving
Thank Him for the joy that comes from open hands

verse.text: Remember this: whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.

blocks.text: Sowing is the farmer's picture of giving: the amount you scatter determines the harvest the field can return. A home that sows sparingly — a little help, a tight budget, a closed door — grows a thin garden. Generosity today plants next season's green.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Decide the family sowing rate: generous, not sparing
Plant something small today that pays in kindness later
Keep the ledger simple: sow, wait, reap — God keeps the books

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make your family sowers of generosity
Thank Him for the harvest He grows from giving

verse.text: At the present time your plenty will supply what they need.

blocks.text: Paul's great sentence: 'your plenty will supply what they need.' The staggering part is the second half — 'so that in turn their plenty will supply what you need.' Generosity is a relay: nobody stays rich permanently, nobody stays in want permanently, and the baton keeps moving.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Look at your plenty and spot one person whose need it fits
Fill it today — food, time, skills, money
Remember you're running a relay, not a race to be first

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to show you whose need your plenty meets
Thank Him for the fellow runners in the relay of grace

verse.text: They all gave out of their wealth; but she, out of her poverty, put in everything... she had to live on.

blocks.text: Jesus watches the offering — the important visitors with the big gifts and the widow with two coins — and declares her the largest giver of the day. Today's quiz is about what Jesus was weighing.

blocks.question: Why did Jesus rate the widow above everyone else?
options: Her two coins were worth more in gold
She gave everything she had to live on — all of it
blocks.explain: Right — the measuring is by self-gift, not by amount. The widow gave her whole living, which is the biggest thing that can be given.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for a heart that gives all it has to live on
Thank Him for the widow's lesson and her Lord

verse.text: Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together and running over.

blocks.text: Jesus promises giving has a return, and He paints it in farmer's language: pressed down, shaken together, running over — a measure that cannot hold everything. On a rest day, rest in the arithmetic of heaven: generosity does not deplete you.

blocks.prompt: Think of a gift your family gave that came back running over. Write it down and give thanks.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the running-over measure of His giving
Ask Him to make your recent kind and generous family

verse.text: In everything set them an example by doing what is good.

blocks.text: A household's generosity is mostly caught, not taught. Children become givers by watching givers. Monday is the day to make yourself an example by doing good — the family is filming every gesture, and the record shows.

blocks.prompt: Write the one act of generosity you want the family to remember you by this week — then go do it today.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make your home an example of good
Thank Him for modelling generosity in His own life

intro.text: The most needed skill in a household is not speaking but listening — to each other, and first to God. This week we practise the habit of the open ear.

verse.text: Speak, LORD, for your servant is listening.

blocks.text: Young Samuel didn't know God's voice yet — but with Eli's help he offered a listening heart. The prayer is the whole of listening to God: 'Speak, LORD, for your servant is listening.' It is the first prayer of every faithful morning.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Begin your day with Samuel's prayer: Speak, LORD, I'm listening
Keep the Bible open — it is where He usually speaks
Ask someone you trust: what do you hear God saying?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask the LORD to speak and give you ears
Thank Him that He is willing to be heard

verse.text: Faith comes from hearing the message, and the message is heard through the word about Christ.

blocks.text: Faith is a listening habit. It is not born from arguments or spectacles but from hearing the message about Christ — again and again and again. A family that faithfully hears the Word is quietly building a household of faith, one hearing at a time.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Hear the Word today — a sentence, a page, a parable
Talk about what you heard at a meal, not just what happened
Trust the slow build: hearing produces faith

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to grow your faith through the Word you hear
Thank Him for speaking through Christ

verse.text: My dear brothers and sisters, take note of this: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to become angry.

blocks.text: James orders a household's three speeds: quick to listen, slow to speak, slow to anger. Most family fights are actually listening failures — two people broadcasting over a closed line. Today, try the reversal: be the one who is quick to listen all day long.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Let someone finish — completely — before you reply
Ask one real follow-up question to show you were listening
Notice how often you were 'quick to speak' and correct it

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for quick ears in your home today
Thank Him for listening to every word you pray

verse.text: The purposes of a person's heart are deep waters, but one who has insight draws them out.

blocks.text: People's hearts are deep water — you can't read what's underneath from the surface. Insight draws it out: gentle questions, unhurried time, patient silence. The people you live with are carrying deep things; listening draws them up where they can be known and loved.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Give one person your full unhurried attention today
Ask a gentle question to draw their heart out
Leave space for silence — the deep water needs it

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for insight to draw out the hearts in your home
Thank Him for drawing out your own heart and knowing it

verse.text: Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.

blocks.text: Jesus ends His parables with an invitation, not a demand: whoever has ears, hear. Hearing is a choice we make to let a word go down deep. Today's quiz is about the soil of the listening heart.

blocks.question: In the parable, which soil actually produces a crop?
options: The hard path where the word lands on top
The good soil that hears, accepts and produces
blocks.explain: Right — deep, receptive hearing produces fruit. Ears are the doorway of the harvest.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Jesus to open your ears to His word
Thank Him for the seed He keeps sowing in your home

verse.text: My sheep listen to my voice; I know them, and they follow me.

blocks.text: Listening to God is not an act of genius but of relationship — like a sheep that knows its shepherd's voice in a field of noise. On a rest day, quiet things down long enough to recognise the one voice that knows you by name.

blocks.prompt: When has you heard the Shepherd's voice most clearly? Write the memory down — the place, the season, the word.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask the Shepherd to make His voice familiar to you
Thank Him that He knows you by name

verse.text: Assemble the people — men, women and children... so they can listen and learn.

blocks.text: Moses' instruction for family worship: gather everyone, so they can listen and learn. Listening was never meant to be solo work. When a household gathers to hear God together, the word lands in ears that will grow it all week.

blocks.prompt: What did your household hear this week that you both want to keep? Choose one verse to repeat until it's everyone's.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the blessing of gathered listening
Ask Him to keep your family's ears open all season

intro.text: No household escapes storms — health, money, tension, loss. This week we practise finding peace not in calm skies but in the God who commands both wind and wave.

verse.text: He said to the wind and the waves, "Peace! Be still!"

blocks.text: The disciples are terrified in a storm, and Jesus — asleep in the boat — wakes, speaks, and the wind and waves obey Him. The point of the story is not that storms won't come; it's that the Person with the power is in your boat.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Say to your storm today: 'Peace, be still' — in Jesus' name
Name the storm honestly, then name the One who is in the boat
Remind each other: He is not afraid of your weather

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Jesus to speak peace over your household's storm
Thank Him that He calms wind and wave with a word

verse.text: Peace I leave with you; my peace I give you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled.

blocks.text: The world's peace comes from circumstances being fixed; Jesus' peace comes from Jesus being present. That is why He can give it in a room where everything is about to go wrong. His peace is not hostage to your weather.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Receive His peace as a gift, not a result of fixing everything
When a trouble knocks, remind yourself: not as the world gives
Let His peace guard one conversation today

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Jesus for the peace only He can give
Thank Him that His peace is not hostage to your news

verse.text: He will cover you with his feathers, and under his wings you will find refuge.

blocks.text: The storm shelter of the Bible is the Presence itself. Frightened children (and grown ones) hide under a parent's wings; the psalmist says that's exactly who God is. In the middle of any weather, there is a place: under His wings.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Picture yourself under His wings — let the body relax into it
Be a shelter under the wing for one frightened person today
Say it: 'He will cover you with his feathers'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Take refuge under His wings today
Thank Him for the shelter of His presence

verse.text: He stilled the storm to a whisper; the waves of the sea were hushed.

blocks.text: The psalmist watches God reduce a storm to a whisper. Peace is not only for the storm — it is also the tone of a household. God can hush the waves outside; you can help hush the noise inside.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Turn something in your home down today — a volume, a pace, a screen
Hush one wave of words instead of riding it
Notice the whisper of God in the quiet you made

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to still the storms in and around your home
Thank Him for the whisper that comes after

verse.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

blocks.text: Peacemaking is not avoiding conflict; it is walking into it with tools of peace. Today's quiz is about which move actually makes peace in a stormy conversation.

blocks.question: Which move turns a family argument toward peace?
options: Walking away and ignoring the conflict
Calmly saying what's true and listening for what's true in reply
blocks.explain: Right — peacemakers face the storm with truth and calm; ignoring it just postpones the bad weather.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to call your house peacemakers
Thank Him that peacemakers are called children of God

verse.text: Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.

blocks.text: Storms wear people out — the worried parents, the anxious children, the ones pretending not to be tired. Jesus invites the weary and burdened to come for rest. On a rest day, the peace is not earned; it is received by coming.

blocks.prompt: Name the burden you've been carrying through this storm. Write it down and, in prayer, put it down at Jesus' feet.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Come to Jesus with your weariness
Thank Him for rest that is a gift, not a reward

verse.text: May the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times and in every way.

blocks.text: Paul calls God 'the Lord of peace himself' — not the giver of a commodity, but the very person of peace. His peace comes 'at all times and in every way', which covers even the Mondays after the storm. Monday is for resting in the Person.

blocks.prompt: Write one line of prayer for your household: 'Lord of peace, give us...' and finish it honestly today.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive peace from the Lord of peace himself
Ask Him for peace at all times and in every way

intro.text: Gratitude is the family thermostat: a grateful home runs warm; an ungrateful one runs cold. This week we practise thankfulness until it becomes the default language of the house.

verse.text: Give thanks in all circumstances; for this is God's will for you in Christ Jesus.

blocks.text: Note the small word: IN all circumstances, not FOR all circumstances. God does not ask you to thank Him for the hard thing — but to find thanks even in hard places, because He is present there too. That single shift changes a household's weather.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name one thank-you you could give even in today's hardest part
Let the kids catch you being grateful out loud
Give thanks in a circumstance you'd rather grumble about

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Give thanks in all your today
Ask God to make thankfulness your family's first language

verse.text: Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights.

blocks.text: James traces every good gift back to one Giver: the Father of lights. Nothing good in your life fell out of a machine — it came down from Him. Gratitude is simply the family habit of acknowledging where the good came from.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Trace the good gifts of today back to their Giver
Say thank you to God out loud, in front of the family
Keep a running gift-list on the fridge — and read it when ungrateful

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank the Father of lights for every good gift
Ask Him to keep your eyes on the Giver, not just the gifts

verse.text: Jesus asked, "Were not all ten cleansed? Where are the other nine?"

blocks.text: Ten lepers are healed; one returns to say thank you. Jesus' question hangs in the air: Where are the nine? Gratitude is the one who comes back. It is the difference between receiving gifts and knowing the Giver.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Be the one who returns: thank someone specifically today
Find the Giver behind one of today's healings
Ask: am I a nine or a one?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Return to Jesus with your thanks today
Thank Him for healing you may have forgot to mention

verse.text: Enter his gates with thanksgiving and his courts with praise; give thanks to him and praise his name.

blocks.text: Psalm 100 makes thanksgiving the entrance: you come into God's presence through gratitude. A household that prays with thanksgiving is a household that keeps finding the door open.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Open prayer with thanks before you ask for anything
Walk through today's 'gate of thanksgiving' to God's presence
Sing a praise — the courts don't mind your voice

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Enter His gates with thanksgiving today
Thank Him for the open door of praise

verse.text: Then Jesus took the loaves, gave thanks, and distributed to those who were seated.

blocks.text: Jesus thanks God over bread and fish — the most ordinary food of the day. Today's quiz is about what Jesus models in that small moment.

blocks.question: Why did Jesus give thanks over the ordinary loaves?
options: To bless the everyday bread, not just the miracles
Only because the crowd was watching
blocks.explain: Right — Jesus habitually blessed the ordinary. Daily bread, lifted with thanks, is holy enough for the whole home.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God over your ordinary bread today
Ask Him to make every meal a small thanksgiving

verse.text: Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts... and be thankful.

blocks.text: Paul ties peace and gratitude to the same heart — the peace of Christ rules where thankfulness keeps house. On a rest day, let the machinery slow and the thanks rise: the two go together like a warm fire and a quiet evening.

blocks.prompt: Write a short list — five small thanks for this week. Read it out loud tonight.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let the peace of Christ rule in your heart
Ask Him to keep your whole family thankful

verse.text: Be thankful.

blocks.text: Two words. Paul closes the peace passage with a command so short it might look like punctuation — but it's the mother tongue in a Christian household. Monday is the day to use it early and often: be thankful. It catches.

blocks.prompt: Say 'thank you' to God and to someone at home before breakfast. Write what happened when you started your day that way.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Speak the language of thanks all day
Thank God for teaching your family its home tongue

intro.text: The final week of spring: everything your household has practised this season is meant to be carried out of the house. Your home was lit for a reason — the light was always going somewhere.

verse.text: Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a bowl. Instead they put it on its stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house.

blocks.text: A lamp that isn't lifted is pointless. Jesus says a family of faith is a lighted lamp — not to stay hidden, but to give light to everyone in the house and beyond it. This week, lift the lamp. Let it be seen.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Sit in the visible place today — don't hide your faith at home or work
Let one good deed of your household be obvious
Ask: who is in the light's reach?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Jesus to put your family's lamp where it helps most
Thank Him for the light He lit in you

verse.text: You are the salt of the earth.

blocks.text: Salt preserves, seasons and makes thirsty. Jesus calls His people salt — meaning a family that tastes of something more, that keeps its corner of the world from going flat and flavourless. You don't have to be loud to be salty; you have to be present and consistent.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Add seasoning: be the reason one gathering felt more alive
Preserve something good today — a friendship, a mood, a memory
Make someone thirsty for the source of your hope

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make your family salt in your neighbourhood
Thank Him for the flavour He gives you

verse.text: Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.

blocks.text: The purpose of visible good deeds is not applause for the family but glory for the Father. When neighbours see kindness without a punchline, they start wondering about heaven. This week, let them wonder — and see.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Do one good deed with no need to be thanked
Do it 'before others' — in the open where it can point to God
Brace for the strange joy of not getting the credit

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to be glorified through your family's good deeds
Thank Him for the light you get to carry

verse.text: A town built on a hill cannot be hidden.

blocks.text: You cannot hide a city on a hill any more than you can hide a lit lamp. Jesus is redefining what a household is for: not a private fortress but a visible landmark — a place that can be found when people are lost.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Be easy to find today — keep doors (behavioural, not just physical) open
Answer honestly when someone asks what your family is all about
Look out over the 'town below' and notice who could use your hill

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make your home a landmark of His grace
Thank Him that the City is not just a dream

verse.text: Do not grow weary in doing good, for you will reap a harvest at the proper time.

blocks.text: Light carried long is light that keeps burning. The danger for a family at the end of a season is tiredness — the sudden urge to put the lamp back under a bowl. Today's quiz tests the final week's antidote.

blocks.question: What is the fix for a light that's feeling weary?
options: Don't give up — the harvest comes at the proper time
Because keeping it is costly, hide it for a while
blocks.explain: Right — weary light is carried by a promise: reaping comes at God's proper time. Keep burning.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to keep your family's light steady
Thank Him for the harvest that waits at the proper time

verse.text: In repentance and rest is your salvation, in quietness and trust is your strength.

blocks.text: Before the light goes down the road, it needs quiet and trust — the resting days of a faithful household. On a rest day, refuel: repentance, rest, quietness, trust. That is the strength tank for carrying the light.

blocks.prompt: What has this season given your household? Write three things you're carrying out of spring into the road ahead.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive quietness and trust as your strength
Thank God for the season He just walked you through

verse.text: Let everything you do be done in love.

blocks.text: The last command of a light-carrying household is the simplest: do everything in love. Not 'do everything perfectly' — in love. That is what makes the light worth carrying, and what keeps it burning after this season is long over.

blocks.prompt: Write your family's one-sentence mission for carrying love into the next season — then pray it out loud tonight.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make love the finish-line of this season
Thank Him for the light of His own love in you
